title: Restricted repertoire at the Hall
summary: Bull notes the Hall repeats tunes such as Bill Bailey and The Saints, and says his disappointment is the administration, not the music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: What about tunes? What sort of tunes do they play there?

Very restricted tunes in a lot of cases. I mean, this I don't mind so much. I don't mind Sweet Emma playing Closer Walk three times a night because I like to hear her sing it every time. But they do play fairly restricted tunes. They play Bill Bailey every night without fail at least once, often twice. They have to play The Saints. Well, I mean, they do sort of in a way have to, and I can understand that because I've had to play The Saints myself when I didn't want to. The bands that play don't really disappoint me. Some musicians in the bands do, and there are other musicians in the city that are better, that aren't used there, and I wish were used there. It's not so much the music that disappoints me as the administration. You know, the situation as it stands with the place and the way it's run. To me, that's a big disappointment.
